question.prompt: The function \(x^2+px+q\) with \(p\) and \(q\) greater than zero has its minimum value when:

solutions.explanation:
Completing the square reveals which part of the expression can vary and how small it can become. For real \(x\),
\[
x^2+px+q=\left(x+\frac p2\right)^2+q-\frac{p^2}{4}.
\]
The square is nonnegative, so the function is at least \(q-\frac{p^2}{4}\). It attains that value exactly when \(x+\frac p2=0\). Therefore the minimum occurs at \(x=-\frac p2\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
solutions.title: Complete the square
